segments: <1>Idea</1><2>You + SPP</2><3>We start with the outcome you want — a launch, a uniform, a campaign — not with a product code.</3>
<1>Design</1><2>SPP designers</2><3>Artwork is drawn for the garment, the substrate and the viewing distance it will actually meet.</3>
<1>Visualise</1><2>SPP Studio</2><3>You see the design on the product, front and back, before anything is made.</3>
<1>Quote</1><2>SPP</2><3>On-site estimates are a guide. The written quote from SPP is the price, with nothing hidden in it.</3>
<1>Approve</1><2>You</2><3>A production proof is sent for sign-off. Nothing is printed until you have approved it.</3>
<1>Produce</1><2>SPP production</2><3>One team and one job number, however many product lines the project touches.</3>
<1>Quality control</1><2>SPP QC</2><3>Every order passes the same checklist before it is packed.</3>
<1>Deliver</1><2>SPP</2><3>Shipped to any province, or installed by our own crews for signage and billboards.</3>
<1>Reorder</1><2>You</2><3>Designs, sizes and specifications stay on file, so the next run is one message — not a new project.</3>
<1>Show it before we make it.</1><2>Mockups, previews and proofs come first. Approvals are faster when nobody has to imagine anything.</2>
<1>Design for the press, not the screen.</1><2>Artwork that ignores production gets rebuilt at the last minute. Ours starts from how it will be made.</2>

<1>Say what is true.</1><2>An estimate is called an estimate. A billboard request is called a request until our team confirms it. Automated artwork checks are advisory, and a person reviews every file.</2>
<1>One job, one owner.</1><2>A shirt, a banner and a billboard for the same launch are one project with one point of contact — not three orders that happen to share a logo.</2>
<1>Make the second order easy.</1><2>The best measure of a production company is whether people come back. We keep what we need on file so that coming back is effortless.</2>
